requirements.requirement: Configure node1 (VyOS) to provide NAT (source masquerade) for the private network toward the internet
requirements.summary: node1 eth1 was addressed 10.50.50.254/24, a source NAT rule 100 masquerading 10.50.50.0/24 out eth0 was committed and saved, a forward filter (default-drop + established/related + eth1-inbound accept) was applied, and ip_forward/per-interface forwarding was confirmed enabled (cmd-070b4a88da52432d, cmd-53c96ec191c44189, cmd-a8e7fbb7fb6447ab, cmd-f79e2e44b791485d, cmd-a0c1b1a8357d4231). Configuration persisted across a reboot (cmd-ac5dcd8095994a93).

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 given private-network addresses and a default route via node1
requirements.summary: systemd-networkd drop-ins created on node2 (10.50.50.11/24) and node3 (10.50.50.12/24), each with a default route via 10.50.50.254 (node1's private-side address); confirmed applied via ip addr/route output (cmd-6627b326d87d4ddd, cmd-abbc231a68ab47bd). Addressing and routing persisted across reboot (cmd-2673fa479ac44f0a, cmd-668fe3ce4b5e4d08).

requirements.requirement: Processes on node2 and node3 can actually reach the internet through node1's NAT
requirements.summary: curl bound to the private interface on both node2 and node3 successfully reached external hosts (301/redirect responses, external IP returned by ipify), and node1 conntrack directly showed the flows from 10.50.50.11/.12 masqueraded to node1's WAN address 10.100.232.10 (cmd-d6b5d3b1b71540d6, cmd-80fb8e130b264c00, cmd-09983b547e494886). Post-restart-cycle conntrack again confirmed simultaneous masqueraded flows from both private hosts (cmd-867bf034c23b4d82).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all three managed nodes (node1, node2, node3) with pre-restart baseline, ack, changed boot identity, and recovered service/connectivity state
requirements.summary: For each node, a pre-restart healthy baseline and boot_id was captured (cmd-26ef1910a42a4328, cmd-3211c6e6ea9f4adc, cmd-5d69e49393eb4ed5), a backgrounded reboot was acknowledged (cmd-c893d0b3e0424ba6, cmd-e8800f2844fb4dba, cmd-e5838e27df4444f5), connection loss and recovery were directly observed via repeated polling that timed out then succeeded (cmd-b837b18d01ce4ba9, cmd-19491921957842ca, cmd-b34d8c2a727047b0, cmd-ebe7bf546e3a40c9, cmd-a6edcf2ed8b64d95, cmd-dd9af046b91b443a), boot_id changed on all three nodes matching the fixed after-executor snapshot (e98d9010→13aedc4e, cfdbaef8→57181c62, 96c08b66→aa5a56bb), and post-restart NAT/private-network configuration and connectivity were re-verified on each node (cmd-ac5dcd8095994a93, cmd-b32ac6f8e309412d, cmd-db1ef8b84ff240b2, cmd-2673fa479ac44f0a, cmd-668fe3ce4b5e4d08), with a final combined conntrack check after all three restarts (cmd-867bf034c23b4d82).

overall_summary: node1 was configured as a working NAT gateway (VyOS masquerade rule plus forward filter) for the 10.50.50.0/24 private network, and node2/node3 received static private addresses with a default route via node1. Direct evidence (curl responses and node1 conntrack entries showing masquerade translation to node1's WAN address) confirms both node2 and node3 can reach the internet through node1. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was completed on all three nodes with pre-restart baselines, reboot acknowledgements, directly observed connection-drop/recovery, boot_id changes matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and re-verified NAT/connectivity state afterward, including a final combined conntrack check. No unnecessary or unrestored mutations were identified.
limitations: No external ground truth (e.g., an independent internet-side observer) was available to corroborate that traffic actually reached the public internet beyond the 301/redirect HTTP codes and conntrack entries captured by the executor.

The lifecycle collector's after_prepare phase is an alias of before_prepare (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before_prepare/after_executor diff, which showed only expected boot-identity, ephemeral socket/PID, and systemd-private tmp-directory changes from the reboots.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing executor commands chronologically. Early NAT configuration attempts on node1 (cmd-070b4a88da52432d) failed on invalid firewall 'state established/related' syntax; these were immediately corrected in follow-up commit commands (cmd-3dc4764548584e96, cmd-a8e7fbb7fb6447ab) with no lingering bad state — normal iterative configuration, not unnecessary mutation. A firewall rule 10 action was deleted and re-set within the same corrective commit (cmd-a8e7fbb7fb6447ab) to fix the earlier partial failure; this is a legitimate correction, fully reflected in the final committed/saved config. Reboots on all three nodes were required by the mandated restart-evidence protocol, not the public task, but are bounded, single actions with full recovery verification and no residue. No unnecessary, unrelated, or unrestored mutations were found (e.g., no stray files, no weakened security controls, no failed services present before or after per the lifecycle snapshots).
